_comment: Which versions of the Void changed which numbers of an analysis (round 67). Columns are the-void-analyze summary columns; a trailing * matches a prefix (guest_*). condition, if present, limits a change to some inputs: not_cif = only structures that were not read from a CIF (a CIF is always read in the standard orientation); has_metal = only structures with one of the listed metals; value_matches = only entries whose value in a column matches one of the listed patterns. A release that changes a number adds a record here, and tests/test_index_staleness.py checks every record names real columns and versions.

changes.what: The channel/pocket split, accessible volume and guest accessibility join the Voronoi network to the grid's percolation: a window only slightly wider than the probe now counts (UiO-66 with N2: channel ASA 0 -> 1093 A2).
Oxalate is a linker, not part of the node, in topology (CALF-20 is dmc).
The PLD rests on a refined network with a proven grid floor, and accessibility uses the same network (a PLD could be too narrow or too wide before).
PLD in layered frameworks from a split-sphere network, and accessibility that agrees with it when nothing percolates.
The split-sphere network is built whenever the atoms' radii differ (3 of 36 CoRE PLDs were 0.18-0.34 A low before).
Surface sampling is drawn in the cell's own frame: a structure not in the standard orientation gave a different ASA (CIF-read structures unchanged).
Surface samples are drawn in a canonical atom order, not file order: every surface area changed within sampling scatter.
Open metal sites are checked on the lanthanides, Y, Th-Pu, In and Ag, with saturated coordination numbers calibrated on CoRE MOF 2024's labels (these metals were not checked before, and counted 0).

Rod SBUs are split at their metals, as CrystalNets and CoRE MOF 2024 do (MIL-53: bpq, not 'not identified'), and nine rod nets joined the bundled library (bpq, rna, pts-x, sea, fgl, ggl, lcv, tfz, nbo-a).
